rationale: Mouse pole performance improved after red pepper decoction and a Parkinson case reported better walking while receiving combination treatment. Neither study counted freezing episodes after eating toasted Sichuan pepper.

A healthy adult extract trial reported lower task fatigue at day 56 after a baseline imbalance. Two gamer registrations add relevant measures without results. The Parkinson outcome after ground pepper remains untested in these sources.

A mixed pepper-oil product improved reported conversation difficulty in xerostomia. A different experiment measured lower-lip tingling. The papers did not measure acoustic loudness or worsening Parkinson’s hypophonia after ground pepper.

A Japanese formula trial found no significant resting pressure change, and an acute allergy case showed severe hypotension. Neither assessed standing symptoms after culinary ground pepper in Parkinson’s.

Insomnia improved during combined formula and rehabilitation treatment in one Parkinson’s case. A healthy gamer extract trial registers sleep disturbance without results. There is no isolated toasted-pepper comparison in these sources.
A Parkinson’s case describes baseline rigidity and improved walking during combination therapy. Related animal motor tests do not quantify rigidity. The direction after ground pepper is unmeasured.
Mouse stress experiments and a Parkinson’s case with cointerventions reported changes in mood-related outcomes. They do not establish what eating toasted pepper does to depression severity.

An extract trial in healthy adults found faster acute attention and fewer false alarms alongside worse name-to-face accuracy. Healthy gamer registrations provide no results, and clinical Parkinson’s attention after toasted pepper remains unresolved.
Combination-treated Parkinson’s cases and related Japanese pepper animal experiments provide no dyskinesia assessment after ground culinary exposure.

Pain outcomes differed across mouse assays and human gastrointestinal studies. The clinical reports used a Japanese-pepper formula or mixed oil, and the mouse study used topical sanshool. Parkinson’s pain after toasted pepper remains unmeasured.
